extracted.intended_audience: general readers and historians interested in early 20th-century Canadian Mounted Police and Yukon/North history
extracted.subtask_description: A narrative/historical excerpt describing actions, reports, patrols, and administrative observations about the Royal North-West Mounted Police (later R.C.M.P.) in the Yukon and other northern/frontier regions in the early 1900s. Emphasizes conduct, patrols, forensic practice, administration, and social interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courage and readiness to confront armed criminals
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers should be willing to confront armed and dangerous individuals directly, often engaging in physical struggle and making arrests under threat of violence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by multiple anecdotes (e.g., Corporal Hogg handcuffing Monaghan who pointed a gun; Corporal Lett grappling the Idaho gunman). These accounts emphasize physical bravery, quick action, and personal risk in effecting arrests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for preventive policing over public spectacle
rubrics_metrics.description: The Force preferred to exercise preventive power — heading off crime quietly rather than seeking dramatic, publicity-generating confrontations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text states they 'never hunted after publicity' and often arrested or disrupted schemes covertly (e.g., discovery and suppression of the 'red' conspiracy at White Horse) because prevention was better for the country even if it brought less public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of emerging forensic methods (finger-printing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt and rely on forensic evidence (finger-prints) to identify suspects and secure convictions when other clues are lacking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Superintendent Wood's pioneer use of a finger-print on a lamp-chimney to single out the thief shows positive evaluation of forensic techniques to make 'it daily more impossible for criminals to ply their trade.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed, practical reporting that can inform civil development
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers' field reports should include careful, practical analysis (e.g., agricultural capability, transport needs) that could influence regional development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Superintendent Constantine's 1907 analysis of the Peace River region argues for railway communication; the author laments such reports being 'buried alive' in government departments instead of being publicized to guide progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial and consistent enforcement of law
rubrics_metrics.description: Police should enforce laws without favoritism, applying the same standards to settlers and immigrants alike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspector Wroughton notes little serious crime and the Mounted Police 'played no favourites' in suppressing gambling and other offences; names in reports show enforcement against 'our own race' as well as others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restraint and avoidance of unnecessary bloodshed
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers should exercise restraint to prevent killing where possible, using patience and supervision rather than immediate lethal force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the handling of the fanatic 'Sharpe'—police adopted a waiting policy because an arrest 'could not be made without shooting' and they chose to avoid bloodshed. The Force's duty is to preserve life when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tactful handling of unusual communities and religious groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Use tact, patience, and non-harsh methods to guide and integrate culturally or religiously distinct groups (e.g., Doukhobors) into orderly citizenship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The police 'used great tact' in rounding up, feeding, and preventing parades that shocked communities, eventually influencing the Doukhobors toward responsibility rather than punishment alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual initiative and reliability in small detachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers must be capable of acting effectively on their own or in very small detachments, showing judgment and independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner Perry praises the Force's 'extraordinary elasticity' and ability to establish many new detachments without increased strength, relying on men competent to act separately and on individual initiative—even 'a squad of one.'

rubrics_metrics.name: High physical endurance and robustness for northern service
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel assigned to northern/sub-Arctic patrols must be of robust health and able to withstand extreme cold, long patrols, and deprivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerous patrol accounts (e.g., pelletier's 3,500-mile year, frozen clothing/bedding problems, fifty-day midwinter patrols) illustrate the physical demands and the costs on officers' health and lives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain training reserves; do not send unready recruits to front-line duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep a cadre of well-trained men at headquarters so that inexperienced recruits are not rushed into emergencies unprepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perry's policy of having 'a goodly number of men always in training at headquarters' is praised as statesman-like to prevent unready men from facing crises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment standard: sobriety and trustworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Select recruits who are sober and trustworthy; those lacking these qualities will be detected and removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner Perry's explicit statement: 'We require sober, trustworthy men; those who are not, only remain in the Force until they are found out.' This is given as a core recruitment criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support civil authorities and public health/administrative ordinances
rubrics_metrics.description: Police should assist in enforcing civil ordinances (e.g., horse-breeders, fire and game, public health) to protect communities and prevent epidemics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner of Agriculture credited the Mounted Police with 'invaluable assistance' enforcing ordinances and patrolling quarantined foreign settlements to prevent disease spread.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assert and maintain jurisdiction in remote/trading areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively assert national jurisdiction in remote regions to prevent external traders or outsiders from undermining laws (e.g., protecting musk-ox, regulating visiting ships).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspectors patrolled Hudson Bay regions to assert Canada's jurisdiction where outside traders encouraged illegal killing or trading, and they prescribed conduct for visiting ships to protect natives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve fairness and notify suspects of rights during arrest procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Arresting officers should follow procedures that safeguard defendants' rights and demonstrate careful, fair law enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted U.S. judge praised that the arresting officer 'promptly notified him that whatever he said would be used against him,' using this as evidence of careful British-system policing and fair treatment in extradition contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compassionate, humane conduct toward colleagues and those in distress
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate self-sacrifice and care for comrades in peril, even at personal risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constable Ford's removing his dry clothes to give to the numb, soaked Reeves and searching all night for the drowned Donaldson is cited as an example of valor and compassionate conduct expected among men in the Force.
